Subject: Kestrel projected ramp — initial sizing worksheet attached

Hey Lina —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, attached is a first-pass capacity model based on the traffic patterns you shared (batch jobs for molecule ranking + a small online inference surface for internal tooling). The attached "kestrel_capacity_model_v1.xlsx" includes three scenarios: baseline, 3x research peak, and phased production ramp. Highlights: 

- Baseline: 4x A100-equivalent (pinned Dedicated pool) to cover overnight batch jobs with comfortable KV cache retention.
- Research peak (ad-hoc): additional transient capacity of 8x that can be served via ephemeral shoulder slab + pre-warmed nodes.
- Prod ramp (Q3->Q4): gradual ramp to 24x A100-eq with staged pinning and autoscale policies for daytime spikes.

I've annotated recommended autoscale triggers (CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, token/sec) and a short failure-fallback: lower-precision quantized variants if we hit sustained >90% saturation.

Attachments: kestrel_capacity_model_v1.xlsx

Next steps: If you and Markus are ok with the scenario assumptions I can loop Karthik to produce a more formal ramp playbook (timed pre-warms, eviction guardrails, preemption tolerance) and Priyom can validate inference performance for your largest model.

Cheers,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few clarifications from our side after walking the team through it: 

1) The molecule ranking batch window is flexible but we prefer completion by 08:00 PT; can you confirm the baseline run duration assumptions?
2) Research spikes are usually short (20–45 minutes) but frequent during new screens — we'd prefer minimal cold-start latency for those.
3) For production, we intend to run a heavier online scoring pipeline that needs 99th pct latency guardrails.

Markus and I reviewed the fallback to quantized models — acceptable but we need SLOs when that path is taken and a clear rollback plan. Also procurement will want a clear definition of preemptible vs reserved capacity and what we can expect for retries if nodes are evicted.

Can Karthik and Priyom draft an ops-level playbook that we can hand to our infra team and procurement? Procurement also requested an itemized monthly committed vs burst cost table.

—Lina

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-06-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel projected ramp — initial sizing worksheet attached

Lina —

I put together a short ops draft below addressing the items you called out. I'll produce a polished PDF once we align on the assumptions. High level:

- Baseline run duration: I used a conservative 4-hour window for the baseline nightly batch to ensure we don't starve daytime workloads. If you need completion by 08:00 PT and the batch can start at 01:00 PT, we can compress by adding transient pre-warms the last hour — cost tradeoff is included in the model.

- Short research spikes (20–45m): Recommended approach is a small, always-ready shoulder pool (2–4 GPUs) plus a fast pre-warm window triggered by queue depth and a warmup token threshold. That keeps cold-starts under ~6s for typical models.

- 99th pct latency for prod online scoring: We'll reserve a guaranteed slab (pin up to 8 GPUs initially) and front it with strict routing (priority tiers) and KV cache locality. For tail protection we can enable a degraded-path policy that routes to a quantized variant with explicit SLOs (we'll document expected latency/quality delta).

- Preemptible vs reserved: Proposed split in draft: 70% reserved (monthly commit) for steady-state prod, 30% transient (ephemeral shoulder + pre-warm) for spikes. Eviction tolerance: transient instances will have a 30s shutdown hook allowing graceful checkpointing; we also recommend client-level retry with exponential backoff and idempotency keys for long-running batch jobs.

Action items I will deliver:
1) Ops playbook (PDF) with explicit trigger charts and pre-warm cadence.
2) Eviction and retry patterns + sample client backoff config.
3) Itemized committed vs burst cost table for procurement (matching the workbook).

I can have the draft to you by EOD Monday (2029-06-17). Priyom, can you validate the model inference time numbers for the 2 largest models and confirm the warmup token assumption?

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi all —

Quick verification from the SE bench: I ran short perf passes on the two largest models you sent (model-alpha, model-beta) with a replica of your token distribution. Results: 

- model-alpha: steady-state throughput ~95 tokens/sec on A100-eq (float16), warm-up to full KV hit-rate ~40–60s depending on prefix reuse.
- model-beta: 210 tokens/sec on A100-eq (float16), warm-up ~20–25s.

Based on those numbers, Karthik's warmup-token threshold looks conservative and will keep cold-starts in-check. For the transient shoulder pool I recommend a 3-GPU minimum to cover simultaneous experiments; if you expect >3 concurrent interactive sessions increase accordingly.

I've attached a quick diagram for pre-warm timing (capacity-ramp-diagram.png) and will sync the perf traces into the shared Drive folder.

Priyom
